about: Catalogue of IB AA SL exam question types, built from the per-part tags of the Math-AA question bank (RktRobinhood/Math-AA---Question-Bank). Structures are described in our own words; no IB text, numbers or images. See curriculum/QUESTION_TYPES.md. Check and regenerate with node tools/question-types.mjs.
partIds: A part ID is the bank question ID plus "." and the part letter (aa-sl-2021-may-tz1-p1-q01.a). Questions with no lettered parts use the bare question ID.

types.name: Straight line from conditions, then use it
types.summary: Build a line from two points, a point and a gradient, a parallel or perpendicular condition, or its two intercepts; then use the line to find an unknown coordinate or an area.
chain: midpoint of a segment (sometimes)
gradient of the segment
parallel or perpendicular gradient
equation of the new line through a given point
substitute a point to find an unknown coordinate, or use the line to find an area
given: equation in y = mx + c or general form
types.asked: A gradient, an equation in a stated form, or a coordinate found from the line.
answerForms: stated form (y = mx + c or ax + by + d = 0 with integer coefficients)
randomise: two integer points, or a point and a gradient p/q
the point the new line passes through
the form the answer must take
which coordinate is unknown in the follow-on part
constraints: integer points and gradients with denominator at most 5
the given gradient is non-zero so the perpendicular gradient exists
when ax + by + d = 0 is asked, scale to integers with a > 0
intercepts must be non-zero when the line is built from its intercepts

types.name: Values, composites and inverse values read from a graph or a table
types.summary: A graph of f (or a table of f and g) is given; read a value, evaluate a composite, read an inverse value backwards, then solve an equation involving the inverse.
chain: read f(a) from the graph or table
evaluate (f o f)(a) or (f o g)(a) by reading twice
read f^-1(b) by going from the y-axis back to x
domain of f^-1 is the range of f
solve f^-1(linear expression) = c by applying f to both sides
types.asked: Single values; one short equation solved by undoing f.
randomise: a piecewise-linear or simple one-to-one graph through grid points
a table of four to six x values with f(x) and g(x)
the linear expression inside f^-1 in the last part
constraints: every queried value lands on a grid point or a table entry
the inner output of a composite is itself an input the graph or table shows
f is one-to-one on the shown domain whenever an inverse is asked
the final equation's solution is an integer

types.name: Inverse as a reflection in y = x
types.summary: Sketch the inverse by reflecting the given graph in y = x, or use that symmetry to shortcut a calculation (equal areas, points on y = x).
chain: sketch f^-1 on the same axes by swapping key points
use the symmetry: intersections of f and f^-1 that lie on y = x, or an area doubled by symmetry
types.asked: A sketch of the inverse, or a value found by using the y = x symmetry.
randomise: the graph's endpoints and intercepts, which swap to (b, a)
whether the follow-on uses the symmetry for an area or a distance
constraints: f is one-to-one on its domain
key points on grid points so the swapped points are easy to check

types.name: Evaluate a function or model at a given input
types.summary: Substitute into a given rule, usually a model in context: the value at time zero, at a stated input, or the y-intercept. Often the first part of a longer question.
chain: evaluate at zero or at a stated input
interpret the value in context
later parts solve an equation or optimise with the same model
types.asked: One value, sometimes compared with a point to say if it lies above or below the graph.
randomise: the model family (polynomial, root, rational, exponential)
constraints: Paper 1 inputs give integers or simple fractions
the input lies inside the stated domain
Paper 2 values are given to 3 s.f.

types.name: Domain and range, including restricted and transformed functions
types.summary: State a range from a vertex, an asymptote or endpoint values, including after a reflection or on a restricted domain; use a range to decide when a composite is defined.
chain: find the vertex, asymptote or endpoint values
state the range
use it: the range of a transformed function, or the condition for g(f(x)) to exist
types.asked: A range or domain, or a bound on a constant.
constraints: endpoints are integers or simple fractions
decide deliberately whether each endpoint is included (the usual error)
for composites, the range of the inner function must meet the domain of the outer one

types.name: Sketch a graph from the GDC on a given domain
types.summary: Draw the graph of a given function on a stated domain from technology, labelling intercepts, turning points and endpoints.
chain: sketch with features labelled
write down the zeros or the maximum
use the graph to solve an equation or inequality, or count solutions
types.asked: A sketch showing the requested features.
randomise: the function family (exponential plus linear, polynomial, bell curve, composite with trig)
constraints: one or two turning points and one to three zeros inside the domain
features far enough apart to tell apart on a sketch
the whole graph fits a sensible window

types.name: Sketch from features found in earlier parts
types.summary: Without a calculator, draw a graph using intercepts, a vertex, stationary points or end behaviour that earlier parts found.
chain: earlier parts find intercepts, vertex or stationary points
sketch showing those features and the domain
types.asked: A sketch with specified features labelled.
randomise: for other families, the features that earlier parts produce
constraints: features at integers or simple fractions
the domain includes every feature the sketch must show

types.name: Zeros and turning points with the GDC
types.summary: Find the zeros, a maximum or a minimum of a given function with technology.
chain: often follows a GDC sketch
the values feed later parts (an interval, a distance, an area)
types.asked: Coordinates of zeros or turning points.
constraints: features are not at simple values, so technology is the intended route
features are well separated
state 3 s.f. and use stored values in later parts

types.name: Intersection of two curves with the GDC
types.summary: Find where two curves meet with technology: two models, a curve and a line, or a function and its inverse; then use the points.
chain: find the intersection points
use them: a distance between points, the limits of an area (5.11), or a time interval in context
types.asked: Coordinates of the intersections, or the time when two models are equal.
constraints: one to three clean crossings in the window
no near-tangent crossings that are hard to see

types.name: Build a new function from given ones and optimise it with the GDC
types.summary: Form the difference of two models, or the distance from a point to a curve, then find its maximum, minimum or zero with technology.
types.skillGap: No curriculum skill names forming a distance or difference function and optimising it; SL2.3.sum-difference covers only the graphing half.
chain: earlier parts set up two models
form the difference or distance function
find its maximum, minimum or zero and interpret
types.asked: The greatest or least value, or when the difference is zero.
constraints: the extreme lies inside the domain, not at an endpoint, unless that is the point
the answer is interpretable in context

types.name: Solve an equation that needs technology
types.summary: An earlier part derives an equation that mixes families (angle and sine, exponential and polynomial); solve it with the GDC and keep the root that makes sense.
chain: show or form the equation from geometry or a model
solve with the GDC
reject roots outside the context's domain
types.asked: The solution in context.
constraints: exactly one root in the context interval, or say which one is wanted
no simple exact root, so technology is genuinely needed

types.name: Form a composite, evaluate it, solve for a parameter
types.summary: Write (g o f)(x) for two given rules, evaluate it, or set it equal to a value and solve for an unknown constant.
chain: write the composite expression
evaluate it at a value or set it equal to a given value
solve for the parameter (often two answers from a square)
or equate coefficients with a given form and solve the resulting quadratic
types.asked: An expression, a value, or the parameter.
randomise: outer rule: linear, quadratic, cubic or trig
constraints: the order of composition is stated clearly (f o g versus g o f is the classic error)
solving gives integers, often a +/- pair
Paper 2 versions may compose with a trig function

types.name: Find an inverse algebraically, with its domain; self-inverse functions
types.summary: Swap and rearrange to find f^-1 for a linear, rational or root function, state its domain and range, show a function is its own inverse, or find a constant that makes it so.
chain: (asymptotes of a rational function)
find f^-1(x)
state its domain and range
show f is self-inverse, or use that to find a constant
(link to reflections in the axes)
types.asked: The inverse expression, its domain or range, or a show-that.
constraints: ad - bc is non-zero
a rational function is self-inverse exactly when d = -a
root functions need a stated domain so the inverse's domain is the original range

types.name: Exponential and log functions as inverses and composites
types.summary: Evaluate an exponential or log function, find its inverse by switching form, evaluate the inverse, simplify a composite of exp and log with log laws, and relate their graphs by transformations.
chain: evaluate f at chosen points
find f^-1 by converting between log and exponential form
evaluate f^-1 at a point
simplify a composite such as f(g(x)) with log laws
describe the transformations linking two exponential or log graphs
(solve an inequality in the composite)
types.asked: Values, the inverse rule, a simplified composite.
randomise: a linear shift inside the function
constraints: evaluation points give integer powers
bases chosen from one family (2, 4, 8) when change of base is the point
the inverse's domain follows from the original range

types.name: Read and convert quadratic forms
types.summary: From a quadratic in factorised, vertex or general form, state the intercepts, axis of symmetry and vertex, or convert to another form.
chain: intercepts from factorised form
axis of symmetry as the midpoint of the roots
vertex
vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k
second root from the axis
y-intercept
then a sketch, an inequality or a tangent
types.asked: Intercepts, the axis, the vertex, or the quadratic in another form.
randomise: integer roots p and q, or integer h and k
which form is given and which is asked
constraints: p + q even so the axis and vertex are integers
a is non-zero
Paper 1 only, so every value is exact

types.name: Find a quadratic from its roots, vertex or points
types.summary: Work out the coefficients of a quadratic from a vertex and a point, the two roots, the axis of symmetry, or two points it passes through.
chain: write it in vertex or factorised form
use a further point to find a
expand if a general form is asked
state the range from the vertex
types.asked: The coefficients, or the equation in a stated form.
constraints: a is a non-zero integer or a simple fraction
the extra point is not the vertex or a root
with two points and a known axis, the system has a unique solution

types.name: Solve a quadratic exactly, in context or in disguise
types.summary: Solve a quadratic by factorising or the formula, reject a root the context rules out, or solve a disguised quadratic by substitution.
chain: form the quadratic from the context (probabilities summing to 1, a sector's area and perimeter)
solve it
reject the root that breaks the context (negative length, probability above 1)
or: solve a quadratic, then reuse it with u = a^x
types.asked: The valid root or roots.
constraints: roots factor nicely on Paper 1
with u = a^x, one root of u is negative so it must be rejected
the context makes exactly one root invalid

types.name: Discriminant conditions on a parameter
types.summary: Use the discriminant to find the values of a constant that give a tangent, two intersections, no roots, or an expression that is always positive.
chain: equate a line and a curve (or combine logs) to show a quadratic
set the discriminant = 0, > 0 or < 0
solve the resulting equation or quadratic inequality in the parameter
combine with an extra condition (same-sign roots, positive constant)
types.asked: A show-that, then the parameter value or interval.
randomise: coefficients with the parameter in b or c
which condition (tangent, two points, none, always positive)
constraints: the discriminant is a quadratic in the parameter with integer roots
say whether the inequality is strict
Paper 2 versions are the same algebra, with a log argument that must stay positive

types.name: Intersect a curve and a line exactly, then use the points
types.summary: Equate a curve (quadratic, rational or log) with a line or a normal, solve the quadratic exactly, then find the points or the distance between them.
chain: equate and rearrange to a quadratic
solve exactly
find the coordinates
find a distance or a difference, often as a surd
types.asked: The points, or a distance in a stated surd form.
answerForms: surd form a times root b
randomise: the stated form of the final answer
constraints: roots are integers or surds with a small radicand
the final surd simplifies

types.name: Solve a quadratic inequality
types.summary: Solve a quadratic inequality from its roots and the shape of the graph, including the largest integer that satisfies a context condition.
chain: rearrange to (quadratic) compared with 0
find the roots
choose the region from the parabola's shape
in context: the largest whole number allowed
types.asked: An interval, or an integer from it.
constraints: roots factor on Paper 1
Paper 2 contexts round to a whole number the right way

types.name: Log of a quadratic: domain, asymptotes, zeros and maximum
types.summary: For a log whose argument is a downward quadratic: the domain comes from a quadratic inequality, the vertical asymptotes sit at its roots, the zeros come from setting the argument to 1, and the maximum comes from the vertex.
types.skillGap: No single skill covers a log whose argument is a quadratic; the parts map to four separate skills.
chain: solve the quadratic and the matching inequality
write down the asymptotes at the roots
zeros: argument = 1, solved exactly
use the vertex to get the maximum, then find the base
types.asked: Interval, asymptotes, exact zeros, the unknown base.
constraints: the vertex value is an integer power of the base
argument = 1 gives surd roots with a small radicand

types.name: Asymptotes and intercepts of (ax + b)/(cx + d)
types.summary: Write down the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and find the axis intercepts of a linear-over-linear function.
chain: vertical asymptote where cx + d = 0
horizontal asymptote y = a/c
x-intercept and y-intercept
then a sketch, the range, or the inverse
types.asked: Asymptote equations and intercept coordinates.
randomise: whether constants are letters to find from a given asymptote
constraints: ad - bc is non-zero
c is non-zero
intercepts are integers or simple fractions

types.name: Sketch a rational function and use the sketch
types.summary: Sketch a rational function with labelled asymptotes and intercepts, then use the sketch: an inequality, the number of solutions with another curve, or the graph of its reciprocal.
chain: asymptotes and intercepts
sketch with both branches
use it: an inequality, the range, the number of intersections with another curve
or sketch the reciprocal of the function
types.asked: A sketch, an interval, or a count.
randomise: the second curve for the counting part
constraints: ad - bc is non-zero
intercepts on grid points or simple fractions
the second curve crosses each branch a clear number of times

types.name: Exponential growth, decay and limited-growth models
types.summary: For a model like A e^(kt) or C + A e^(-kt): the initial value, k from a data point or half-life, a prediction, the time to reach a level, the long-run value, and the meaning of the growth factor.
chain: initial value at t = 0
find k from a second data point (show the exact form)
predict at a later time
solve for the time to reach a level, or an inequality for whole time units
long-run value from the horizontal asymptote
interpret the growth factor or rate
types.asked: Values, k, times, the long-run value, an interpretation.
constraints: the threshold sits between the initial value and the limit
times come out positive
the base e or a growth factor (like 1.0x) as the context suggests

types.name: Log function features: asymptote, domain and sign
types.summary: State the vertical asymptote or domain of a transformed log function, or use where ln x is positive or negative.
chain: usually the 1-mark opener of a Section B log question
later parts combine logs into a quadratic or an inequality
types.asked: An asymptote equation, a domain, or where an expression is positive.
constraints: the argument's zero is a simple fraction

types.name: Describe the transformations between two graphs
types.summary: Say which stretches, reflections and translations map one graph onto another, or find the parameter values; includes using log laws to rewrite a log graph as a transformed one.
chain: (rewrite the new function with log laws or by factoring)
name each transformation with its scale factor or vector
state the order where it matters
types.asked: A description in words, or the parameter values.
constraints: at most three transformations
when the order matters, the question says so
log-law versions use bases where the stretch factor is an integer

types.name: Apply transformations to a graph
types.summary: Sketch the transformed graph from the graph of f, or write the new function and state its domain.
chain: apply the transformations to key points
sketch, or write g(x)
state the new domain or range
types.asked: A sketch, a rule for g, or its domain.
constraints: image points land on grid points
at most two transformations on Paper 1
